from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(1)

    def construct(self):

            "A vector splits into horizontal, vertical parts.",

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition: The Parallelogram Rule", [
            "Add vectors head-to-tail for sum.", 
            "Parallelogram rule shows the resultant path.", 
            "Boat speed plus river current vectors."
        ])
        
        # Vectors
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#00CED1", buff=0)
        w = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color="#00CED1", buff=0)
        v_label = MathTex("v", color="#00CED1").next_to(v.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1)
        w_label = MathTex("w", color="#00CED1").next_to(w.get_center(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        v_group = VGroup(v, v_label)
        w_group = VGroup(w, w_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.place_at_grid(v_group, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(w_group, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(v_group), Create(w_group))
        
        # Slide w to head of v
        w_moved = w.copy()
        w_moved.shift(v.get_end() - w.get_start())
        w_moved_label = w_label.copy().next_to(w_moved.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(w.animate.shift(v.get_end()), w_label.animate.next_to(w_moved.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")
        resultant = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=v.get_end() + w.get_end(), color="#FF4500", buff=0)
        res_label = MathTex("v+w", color="#FF4500").next_to(resultant.get_center(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(resultant), Write(res_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        # No extra animation needed for the 3rd point as per prompt constraints
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication and Scaling", [
            "Scalar multiplication scales vector length.",
            "Positive scalars preserve original direction.",
            "Double speed boosts length to 2v."
        ])
        
        # Define objects

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Why Vectors Matter", [
            "Vectors are fundamental in physics.", 
            "Modern software relies on vector math.", 
            "They mathematically describe all motion."
        ])
        
        # Define mobjects once
        v_arrow = Vector(UP * 1.5 + RIGHT * 1.5, color=WHITE)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=WHITE).next_to(v_arrow, UP)
        vector_group = VGroup(v_arrow, v_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_in_area(vector_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(vector_group)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        # Move vector to simulate motion
        self.play(vector_group.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1 + DOWN * 0.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space
outline.target_audience: High school students or introductory undergraduate students

sections.title: Introduction: Scalars vs. Vectors
sections.content: Define a scalar (magnitude only) and a vector (magnitude and direction). Visualize vectors as directed line segments (arrows) in a 2D coordinate plane.
sections.example: Comparing a cat's weight (scalar: 5kg) vs. the cat's velocity as it jumps (vector: 3m/s towards the couch).

sections.title: Vector Representation and Components
sections.content: Introduce Cartesian coordinates (x, y). Explain how a vector is decomposed into its horizontal and vertical components. Show the 'head-to-tail' visualization.
sections.example: A robot moving 3 units right and 4 units up; representing this as the vector [3, 4] starting from the origin.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Parallelogram Rule
sections.content: Demonstrate how to add two vectors by placing the tail of the second at the head of the first. Use the parallelogram animation to show the resultant vector.
sections.example: A boat heading across a river: one vector is the boat's engine speed, the other is the river's current. The resultant vector shows the actual path taken.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication and Scaling
sections.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its length (magnitude) without changing its direction (unless the scalar is negative).
sections.example: A character in a game moving at speed 'v'. If the character gets a speed boost, the vector becomes '2v', doubling the length of the arrow while pointing in the same direction.

sections.title: Conclusion: Why Vectors Matter
sections.content: Summarize that vectors are the building blocks for modern physics, computer graphics, and machine learning. Emphasize that they allow us to describe motion and space mathematically.
sections.example: Connecting the lesson to real-world technology: how 3D animation software uses vector math to rotate characters and track their movement in virtual space.
